meta.description: FLUX.2 Klein 9B character LoRA (preset k9b_laptop_char_lora; LoKr twin: k9b_laptop_char_lokr) in the 16 GB laptop memory profile (RTX 5080 Laptop 16 GB, 96 GB system RAM, native Windows), trained at 1024. SOURCE: the memory settings are COMMUNITY-DERIVED 16 GB settings (ostris/ai-toolkit issues #653 and #669, community Klein low-VRAM guides), NOT measured on the laptop and NOT reproduced in this fork - the fork's last laptop record for Klein is an OOM without layer offloading (batchAdvisor LAPTOP16, variant not recorded). Treat the headroom as inferred and run a short test first. RANK: LoRA rank 32 / alpha 32 (linear only, no conv - the parent k9b_char_lora is linear-only), raised from the parent's 16/16 in v1.1 (2026-10-12) because it matches Adam's earlier Klein 9B runs in this fork (all three used 32/32) and BFL's guidance of rank 32 for complex subjects. NOT compared against 16 at 1024 - no A/B exists. Costs an estimated few hundred MB of VRAM over 16. Otherwise TRAINING MATH IS INHERITED UNCHANGED from k9b_char_lora v1.2: adamw8bit at LR 1e-4, bf16, sigmoid timesteps, batch 1 x accum 1, 1500 steps, caption dropout 0.05 (BFL-published Klein defaults; not 9B-measured). DELTAS, all memory/IO except resolution: (1) resolution [1024] ONLY - the parent's 768 bucket is dropped on purpose (multi-aspect buckets around 1024 stay on). (2) layer_offloading on: text encoder 100%, transformer 80% streamed from system RAM. The fp8 9B transformer is ~9 GB; at 80% about 2 GB stays resident, leaving most of the card for 1024 activations (4096 image tokens) with gradient checkpointing. Community #669 reports a 9B run at 100% offload sitting at ~14.6 GB on a 16 GB card, but that was an edit LoRA with control images (about double the sequence length), so plain character training should have more room - 80% leans high without paying the full 100% speed cost. (3) Text embeddings cached and the text encoder unloaded (cache_text_embeddings + unload_text_encoder), so Mistral is not resident while training; this makes caption dropout a no-op and is mutually exclusive with diff_output_preservation. Latents cached to disk and served from RAM. (4) Sampling DISABLED by default (train.disable_sampling) - on a 16 GB card the sampler, not the training loop, is the VRAM peak. The sample block is kept at 1024 with five [trigger] prompts so you can turn it on, but expect it to spike memory; the intended workflow is train with sampling off, then test the kept checkpoints. max_step_saves_to_keep 10 (save every 250) so every checkpoint of a run up to 2500 steps is kept. QUANTIZATION: quantize + quantize_te with qtype qfloat8 as in the parent - but layer_offloading silently rewrites qfloat8 -> torchao float8 for both (toolkit/config_modules.py ~772-775), so the run will use float8, not quanto qfloat8. That is upstream behaviour, not a preset bug. LOADING (#653): the fork's flux2 load path no longer moves the whole bf16 transformer to the GPU before quantizing - it loads on CPU and quantizes block-by-block on the GPU, then hands the blocks to the layer offloader, so the issue-#653 load-time OOM should not apply (read from code, not tested on 16 GB). WINDOWS: set NVIDIA Control Panel > Manage 3D settings > CUDA - Sysmem Fallback Policy = Prefer No Sysmem Fallback (for the trainer's python.exe or globally). Without it a config grazing the ceiling does not OOM - it spills into shared memory and step time jumps several-fold (#669: ~15 -> 50-90 s/it). If s/it suddenly balloons, you are spilling, not compute-bound. Keep ~1.5 GB VRAM free. IF YOU OOM, in order: (1) confirm sampling is still off; (2) raise layer_offloading_transformer_percent 0.8 -> 1.0; (3) set cache_latents false (keep cache_latents_to_disk) to give back RAM-served latents; (4) drop rank 32 -> 16 (small saving); (5) only then lower resolution to 768 - that last step changes the recipe. If it fits with headroom, lower the transformer percent toward 0.6 for speed. STEPS: meta.step_table below is the fork's existing Klein 9B rule (60 steps/image, clamped 1000-2500, stepSuggestion.ts ARCH_HEURISTICS) written out as points - 17 images ~1000, 20 ~1200, 30 ~1800, 40 ~2400, 42+ capped at 2500. No fork doc gives a reason to change it at 1024 (BFL's 1500-step starting point and 1000-1750 peak are not resolution-split), so the numbers are deliberately UNCHANGED from the per-arch rule; the panel labels it 'preset step table' and divides by effective batch. Other Klein presets keep the per-arch advisor. BATCH: batch 1 recommended. The Machine: 16 GB laptop plan treats batch 1 as an UNMEASURED attempt when layer_offloading is on (the recorded OOM was without it); effective batch above 1 goes through gradient_accumulation. Set your Trigger Word in the job form; the sample prompts use [trigger]. Gated on HF - accept the licence. STEP TABLE (meta.step_table, 2026-10-12, machine-independent - the same table ships on every klein preset, laptop or desktop): 17 images ~1020, 20 images ~1200, 30 images ~1800, 40 images ~2400, 42 images ~2500, exact-count interpolation between rows, capped at 2500 steps. OPTIMIZED DATASET COUNT ~42 images: that is where the cap is reached; past it the panel keeps 2500 and the exposure gauge says the dataset is past the optimal size for this model and suggests curating down, instead of calling it undertrained. Source: BFL's Klein training docs (start at 1500 steps for 20-50 images; LoRAs peak at 1000-1750) with the fork's 60 steps/image rule; community Klein 9B LoKr runs report near-full likeness at 1000-1500 steps on 20 images (r/StableDiffusion). Klein keeps its own 2500 plateau - below the 3000 general cap - because that is the published Klein ceiling. Values are steps at effective batch 1; the Step Suggestion panel divides by your effective batch (batch_size x gradient_accumulation), which is the only thing that differs between machines. Below the first row the first row's steps apply.
